subject: How to perform test-retest using lavaan

messages.author: 6db3c86d422c5ae9
messages.subject: How to perform test-retest using lavaan
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am testing the reliability of my scale using test-retest method. My scale was administrated at two time points which are wave 1 and wave 2. My model is
     model<-"Ag=~ ag1 + ag2 + ag3
                  At=~at1 + at2 + at3 + at4
                  Ag~~At"
Does anyone know how to calculate the correlation coefficient relating to the model between wave 1 and wave 2 using lavaan package?
I would appreciate any help!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: How to perform test-retest using lavaan
parts: Does anyone know how to calculate the correlation coefficient relating to the model between wave 1 and wave 2 using lavaan package?

In the model summary, ask for the standardized results:

fit <- cfa(model, data, ...)
summary(fit, standardized = TRUE)

In the column "std.all", the estimated covariance Ag~~At will be the factor correlation.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

parts: With only two indicators per factor, you have no more information left to identify residual correlations.  In fact, the model is only identified if the factor correlation is substantially nonzero.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: How to perform test-retest using lavaan
parts: Could you please show me the difference between these outputs. Which test results, from cfa or cor.test, is more reliable?

All the results are valid, they are just correlations between different variables.  The latent variables in your lavaan model are not the same as the sum scores ag1 and ag2.  One pair has measurement error, the other pair does not.  You might want to read an introductory textbook on Factor Analysis before drawing any inferences from this type of model.

Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
